name: Haldensee
kurzbeschreibung: Lake Haldensee at 1,124 m above sea level in the Tannheimer Tal: crystal-clear mountain and swimming lake between Grän and Nesselwängle with the Haldensee Water World leisure facility.
beschreibung:
Overview

The picturesque Haldensee is located at an altitude of 1,124 meters above sea level in the heart of Tyrol's Tannheimer Tal – one of Europe's most beautiful high valleys in the Reutte district (Außerfern). Nestled between the traditional mountain communities of Grän and Nesselwängle, the crystal-clear water extends over an area of approximately 73 hectares and reaches a depth of up to 22 meters. Framed by the bold limestone cliffs of the Tannheimer Mountains – including the world-renowned climbing peaks Rote Flüh, Gimpel, and Krinnenspitze – Lake Haldensee combines untouched alpine nature with first-class leisure activities for swimmers, water sports enthusiasts, and leisurely hikers.

Route & Requirements

Lake Haldensee was formed during the last ice age when powerful glacial erosion carved out the natural high basin. Fed by clean mountain streams, the lake is characterized by outstanding water quality of class I. Thanks to its sunny location on the high plateau, the water surface warms up to a pleasant 20 to 24 °C in the peak summer months of July and August, making Haldensee one of the most popular swimming lakes in Western Austria.

Visit & Arrival

The lakeside path and the free sunbathing areas on the eastern shore are freely and cost-free accessible all year round. The Wasserwelt Haldensee outdoor pool is open daily from 09:00 to 18:30 during good swimming weather from late May to early September. Water World admission prices (as of season 2025/2026): Day ticket adults approx. €7.50 (with the regional Tannheimer Tal guest card approx. €6.50), children approx. €4.00, family tickets from €18.00. Arrival by car: From the north toll-free via Füssen or Pfronten (Germany) into the Tannheimer Tal on the B199 to Haldensee/Grän; from the south/Tyrol via the Inntal motorway A12 to Imst/Reutte and over the Fernpass (B179) to Weißenbach and up the B199 into the valley. Large paid parking lots are available directly at the Water World and on the eastern shore. By public transport: Train to Sonthofen station (Bavaria) or Reutte in Tyrol, from there VVT bus line 120 runs frequently directly to the Haldensee Seestraße stop.

Tips

The five-kilometer circular lake path is almost entirely flat, gravelled, and asphalted, making it ideal for wheelchair users, seniors, and families with strollers. After circling the lake, the lakeside restaurant with its sun terrace on the western shore invites you to enjoy fresh Tyrolean lake trout and homemade cakes. At sunrise, the Rote Flüh is spectacularly reflected in the calm water – an absolute insider tip for nature photographers.
preis: Shore and circular path freely accessible; Water World Haldensee outdoor pool approx. €7.50
